_comment: AI-DEV enforcement floor. Deployed to /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.d/20-ai-dev-security.json by `make -C ~/.ai-dev sync` (needs sudo). Managed booleans cannot be overridden by user or project settings, so a checked-out repository cannot switch the sandbox off, re-enable the unsandboxed escape hatch, or unblock credential paths. Deny entries merge from every scope and can only ever narrow access. Remove with `make -C ~/.ai-dev unmanage`.
_note_requiredMinimumVersion: A control that a build silently ignores is not a control. sandbox.network.strictAllowlist arrived in Claude Code 2.1.219; on anything older the key parses, is discarded, and the network posture falls back to PROMPTING for a host outside allowedDomains — which a non-interactive sandboxed command has nothing to answer with, so an off-allowlist host stays reachable and only the explicit deniedDomains entries are refused. Nothing reports that: the settings file still says strictAllowlist:true. Downgrading Claude Code, or deploying this floor onto a machine that never upgraded, would therefore remove the network control while leaving every sign of it in place. requiredMinimumVersion turns that silent degradation into a refusal to start, with a message naming the version. It is enforced ONLY from managed (policy) settings, which is why it lives here and not in the user fragment. Verified in the 2.1.232 binary: the check runs before the session and exits 1 — and `claude update`, `claude install` and `claude doctor` are exempt from it, so a machine pinned below the floor can still upgrade its way out. Raise this number when a newly load-bearing setting needs a newer build; never lower it to make a machine start.
_note_disableBypassPermissionsMode: Claude Code documents this as: 'To prevent bypassPermissions or auto mode from being used, set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode or permissions.disableAutoMode to "disable" in any settings file. These are most useful in managed settings where they can't be overridden.' A launcher-side flag check is a blacklist on one entry point; this is enforcement. It refuses bypassPermissions however it is reached: --permission-mode bypassPermissions in either spelling, --dangerously-skip-permissions, --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions and the Shift+Tab cycle, a defaultMode in any settings file, and bare `claude` invoked without the launcher at all. disableAutoMode is deliberately NOT set: auto is the AI-DEV default mode.
